welcome.worktrees.2:
No git repository found in this workspace.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
welcome.projects.1:
Manage several repositories in this window.
[Add Project](command:worktreeGraph.addProject)
welcome.issues.1:
Issues from the repository's GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps, from Jira and from Redmine, to start work in a worktree with Claude.
[Connect to Remote](command:worktreeGraph.connectHosting)
[Connect to GitLab (URL)](command:worktreeGraph.connectGitLab)
[Connect to Jira](command:worktreeGraph.connectJira)
[Connect to Redmine](command:worktreeGraph.connectRedmine)
welcome.tasks.1:
Tasks queued for the agents, per worktree. When the agent finishes one, the next is sent automatically.
[Add Task](command:worktreeGraph.tasks.add)
[Try Several Approaches](command:worktreeGraph.attempts.try)
welcome.schedules.1:
No schedules. Send tasks to the agents at fixed times (daily, weekdays, every N hours or cron).
[New Schedule](command:worktreeGraph.schedules.new)
welcome.mergeQueue.1:
Branches enter the base one at a time: the base is brought in, the tests run, and only then does the merge happen.
[Add a Branch to the Queue](command:worktreeGraph.mergeQueue.add)

config.baseBranch.description: Base branch (e.g. master). Empty = detected from origin/HEAD, then main/master/develop.
config.worktreeRoot.markdownDescription: Folder where new worktrees are created (e.g. `G:\worktrees`). Empty = `<repo>.worktrees` next to the repository.
config.postCreateCommand.description: Command run in a terminal right after a worktree is created (e.g. npm install).
config.agents.markdownDescription: Agent CLIs offered by the **Agent** button. The first one is the default. Use `{prompt}` in the command to type the task before opening (e.g. `claude {prompt}`). The terminal receives `WTGRAPH_BRANCH`, `WTGRAPH_BASE` and `WTGRAPH_WORKTREE`. `promptCommand` (optional) is used when the extension sends a ready-made task (e.g. resolve a conflict): `{prompt}` becomes the text.
config.agentWhenOpen.description: What the ✦ button does when the agent is already open in the worktree. Ctrl/Alt+click on ✦ always opens another one.
config.agentWhenOpen.enumDescriptions.0: Ask: go to one of the terminals already open or open another one.
config.agentWhenOpen.enumDescriptions.1: Bring the agent's most recently opened terminal to the front.
config.agentTerminalLocation.enumDescrip: In the terminal panel, at the bottom.
As an editor tab, in the active editor group.
config.noFastForwardIntoBase.description: Use --no-ff when merging a branch into the base, preserving the branch's 'shape' in the history.
config.migrations.checkOnMerge.descripti: Before a merge, check whether new migrations on both sides collide (Django, Alembic, Flyway, golang-migrate and numbered files in migrations folders) and offer to rechain the branch's migrations after the target's.
config.migrations.rechainOnSync.descript: During auto sync, rechain (with a commit) the branch's migrations after the base's before merging it. When off, sync stops and warns.
config.graph.maxCommits.description: Number of commits loaded in the graph.
config.graph.showRemoteBranches.descript: Show remote branches in the graph.
config.refreshIntervalSeconds.descriptio: Automatic refresh interval (changes made by agents in other worktrees).
config.statusRefresh.activeSeconds.descr: Maximum age of the git status for worktrees in use (this window, favorite, with an open agent or with changes).
config.statusRefresh.idleSeconds.descrip: Maximum age of the git status for the other worktrees.
config.gitConcurrency.description: How many git processes run in parallel when loading worktree details.
config.autoSync.enabledByDefault.descrip: Whether auto sync starts on in new repositories. After that, the on/off button applies per repository.
config.autoSync.where.description: Default location where base sync runs. The panel's 'where' button chooses per repository.
config.autoSync.where.enumDescriptions.0: Only the extension syncs, in this machine's worktrees.
config.autoSync.where.enumDescriptions.1: Only CI (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, generated by Generate CI); the extension only shows the status.
config.autoSync.where.enumDescriptions.2: Local for unpublished branches, CI for published ones.
config.autoSync.where.enumDescriptions.3: Both, on all branches (may produce duplicate merges).
config.autoSync.mode.description: What auto sync does when the base moves.
config.autoSync.mode.enumDescriptions.0: Merges the base automatically into clean worktrees.
config.autoSync.mode.enumDescriptions.1: Only warns that the branch fell behind, with a button to merge.
config.autoSync.trigger.description: When local sync merges the base into the branches.
config.autoSync.trigger.enumDescriptions: The base is merged into the branch only when it is pushed by the extension; the periodic check only updates the status.
The base is merged into clean worktrees on every check (autoSync.intervalSeconds).
config.autoSync.branches.description: Branch patterns that take part in sync (* = one segment, ** = anything). E.g. ["feat/**", "ai/**"].
config.autoSync.exclude.description: Branch patterns that are never synced.
config.autoSync.fetchRemote.description: Run git fetch on every check and sync from origin/<base> instead of the local base.
config.autoSync.testCommand.description: Verification command run in the worktree after the merge (e.g. npm test). Empty = no verification.
config.autoSync.testTimeoutSeconds.descr: Maximum time for the verification command.
config.autoSync.rollbackOnTestFailure.de: Undo the merge (git reset --keep) when verification fails.
config.flow.markdownDescription: Environment flow in promotion order, e.g. `["develop", "qa", "homolog", "main"]` or objects `{ "branch": "qa", "label": "QA" }`. Empty = uses what was saved by the *Configure Environment Flow* command. The first stage becomes the base, unless `baseBranch` is set.
config.remote.description: Remote used for push and for PRs/MRs.
config.gitlab.hosts.markdownDescription: Self-hosted GitLab addresses, e.g. `https://gitlab.company.com`, `https://git.company.com:8443` or `https://company.com/gitlab` (installed under a subpath). The *Connect to GitLab (URL and Token)* command fills this in. Hosts with "gitlab" in the name are recognized automatically.
config.gitlab.apiUrl.markdownDescription: GitLab API URL, if it is not `<host>/api/v4`.
config.github.apiUrl.markdownDescription: GitHub Enterprise API URL, if it is not `<host>/api/v3`.
config.prompts.resolveConflict.markdownD: Task sent to the agent by the *Resolve with …* button. Placeholders: `${branch}`, `${base}`, `${files}`.
config.prompts.mergeIntoBase.markdownDes: Task sent to the agent when a conflict appears while merging the branch into the base. Placeholders: `${branch}`, `${base}`, `${files}`.
config.redmine.url.description: Redmine address (e.g. https://redmine.company.com). The API key is kept in VS Code's secret storage (Connect to Redmine command).
config.redmine.projectId.description: Project identifier in Redmine. Empty = all projects.
config.issues.branchPrefix.description: Prefix of the branch created for GitHub/GitLab issues (Redmine ones use "redmine").
config.prompts.issue.markdownDescription: Prompt sent to the agent when starting an issue. Empty = default. Variables: `${key}`, `${title}`, `${body}`, `${url}`, `${branch}`, `${base}`.
config.claude.configDir.markdownDescript: Claude Code data folder. Empty = `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude`.
config.claude.showUsageInStatusBar.descr: Show estimated usage (5-hour window and week) in the status bar.
config.claude.sessionBudgetTokens.descri: Token budget for the 5-hour window, to show the percentage used (0 = don't show). The official limits are not stored on disk; calibrate using Claude Code's /usage.
config.claude.weeklyBudgetTokens.descrip: Weekly token budget, to show the percentage used (0 = don't show).
config.claude.weekStart.description: How to count the week in the estimated usage.
config.claude.maxSessionsPerGroup.descri: How many sessions to show per worktree in the Claude Sessions view.
config.prompts.fixPipeline.markdownDescr: Task sent to the agent by *✦ Fix* on a failed pipeline. Empty = default text. Placeholders: `${branch}`, `${pipeline}`, `${url}`, `${jobs}`, `${log}` (last ~150 lines of the failed job).
config.checks.mode.description: What happens when the checks before merging or pushing fail.
config.checks.mode.enumDescriptions.0: A failure blocks the merge/push (you can still continue by confirming).
config.checks.beforeMerge.markdownDescri: Commands run in the source branch's worktree before merging it (e.g. `["npm run lint", "npm test"]`). Not run when it is the base coming down into a work branch.
config.checks.beforePush.description: Commands run in the branch's worktree before pushing and before opening a PR/MR.
config.checks.useTestCommand.markdownDes: When no commands are configured, use `worktreeGraph.autoSync.testCommand` for the checks.
config.checks.timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum time for each check command.
config.prompts.fixChecks.markdownDescrip: Task sent to the agent by "✦ Fix" when the checks fail. Placeholders: `${branch}`, `${action}`, `${commands}`, `${failed}`, `${log}`. Empty = default text.
config.protectedBranches.markdownDescrip: Protected branches (accepts `*`/`**`). Empty = automatic: the base, the environment flow stages, `main` and `master`.
config.protection.mode.description: How to handle direct merges and pushes to protected branches. A force push to a protected branch only goes through with "off".
A direct merge/push to a protected branch asks you to type the branch name.
Direct merge/push blocked; offers to open a PR/MR.
config.cleanup.remindThreshold.descripti: Warn when there are at least this many merged and idle (or orphaned) worktrees.
config.cleanup.staleDays.description: Days without a commit for a merged worktree to count as idle.
config.prompts.review.markdownDescriptio: Task sent to the agent by *Review PR/MR with the Agent*. Empty = default text. Placeholders: `${kind}`, `${title}`, `${url}`, `${branch}`, `${base}`, `${diffStat}`. The agent must write `.worktree-graph/review.json` in the format `{ summary, comments: [{ path, line, severity, body }] }`.
config.claude.pricePerMTokInput.markdown: US$ per million input tokens (and cache creation), for the estimated cost per task. 0 in all = no cost estimate.
config.claude.pricePerMTokOutput.markdow: US$ per million output tokens, for the estimated cost per task. 0 in all = no cost estimate.
config.claude.pricePerMTokCacheRead.mark: US$ per million cache read tokens, for the estimated cost per task. 0 in all = no cost estimate.
config.agents.idleMinutes.description: Minutes without changes to the worktree's HEAD or index before the agent is considered finished (when the end of the command can't be detected by shell integration).
config.agents.notifyReady.description: Notify when an agent finishes and the worktree is ready for review.
config.tasks.autoAdvance.description: When the agent finishes a queued task, send the next one automatically.
config.fetch.intervalMinutes.description: Automatic fetch every N minutes (0 = off), with a notice when branches get updates on the remote.
config.bitbucket.hosts.markdownDescripti: Bitbucket Server/Data Center hosts, e.g. `git.company.com` or `https://git.company.com/bitbucket` (with the context path, if any). Addresses with "bitbucket" in the name are recognized automatically.
config.azureDevOps.hosts.markdownDescrip: Azure DevOps Server (on-premises) hosts, e.g. `tfs.company.com`. dev.azure.com and *.visualstudio.com are recognized automatically.
config.azureDevOps.workItemType.descript: Type of work item created by "New Issue…" in Azure DevOps (Task, Bug, User Story, Issue…).
config.jira.url.description: Jira address (Cloud or Server/Data Center). Credentials are kept in VS Code's secret storage (Connect to Jira command).
config.jira.projectKey.description: Jira project key (e.g. PROJ). Empty = the one chosen when connecting.
config.jira.jql.markdownDescription: Optional JQL that replaces the default filter (project and `statusCategory != Done`). For "mine", the extension appends `assignee = currentUser()`.
config.jira.issueType.description: Issue type created by "New Issue…" in Jira.
config.ciBranches.markdownDescription: Extra branches for the history's **CI** filter (in addition to those found in the environment flow, the base and the CI files: `.github/workflows`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`). Accepts patterns with `*`.
config.pushStatusBar.markdownDescription: Shows the **☁ Push** button in the status bar: pushes the branches chosen from a list in which the base and the CI branches (the same as the **CI** filter, including `#worktreeGraph.ciBranches#`) come preselected. The number next to it is how many of them have commits to push.
config.agentStatusBar.markdownDescriptio: Shows the **✦ agent** button in the status bar (the first of `#worktreeGraph.agents#`), which opens the agent in a terminal in this window's worktree.
config.worktreeStatusBar.markdownDescrip: Shows in the status bar which worktree (folder) and branch this window is on. Click to open the panel.
config.mergeQueue.pushBase.description: Merge queue: push the base after each merge.
config.batch.maxParallel.description: Batch task: how many agents are open at the same time; the rest wait for a free slot.
config.budget.perWorktreeTokens.descript: Token budget per worktree (0 = no limit). Warns at 80% and 100%.
config.budget.perWorktreeUsd.description: US$ budget per worktree (0 = no limit; uses the prices from worktreeGraph.claude.pricePerMTok*).
config.budget.action.description: What to do when a worktree exceeds its budget.
config.budget.action.enumDescriptions.1: Warns and stops sending queued/scheduled tasks to the worktree that exceeded it.
config.taskTemplates.markdownDescription: Extra task templates `{ name, description?, prompt }`. Placeholders: `${branch}`, `${base}`, `${file}`, `${selection}`, `${issue}`. Files in `.agentyard/templates/*.md` in the repository also count.
config.readySummary.enabled.description: Show the summary (commits, files, +/−) when an agent becomes ready for review.
config.readySummary.useAgent.markdownDes: Also ask the agent for a summary (what changed, risks, what to test) in `.worktree-graph/summary.md`, outside git.
config.env.ports.markdownDescription: Ports per worktree, e.g. `{ "base": 3000, "step": 10, "vars": ["PORT", "VITE_PORT", "API_PORT"] }`. Each worktree gets a stable block; the 1st variable gets the port, the following ones +1, +2…
config.env.devCommand.description: Development command run by "Run Dev" (e.g. npm run dev), with the worktree's port variables.
config.setup.nodeModules.description: What to do with Node dependencies when creating a worktree (postCreateCommand, if set, takes precedence).
config.setup.nodeModules.enumDescription: Install the dependencies in a terminal.
config.diskUsage.enabled.description: Calculate each worktree's disk usage in the background.
config.diskUsage.secondsPerWorktree.desc: Maximum time to measure a worktree's disk usage (beyond that, the value is a minimum).
config.report.agentSummary.description: In the Daily Report, offer "✦ Draft Summary with the Agent".
config.pullRequests.mergeMethod.descript: Method used when merging a PR/MR from the Pull Requests view (GitLab doesn't rebase from here: it uses merge).

config.claude.trackState.markdownDescrip: Opens Claude Code with hooks (via `--settings`, without touching your `settings.json`) so AgentYard knows when each one is working, waiting for your permission, or done with its turn. Hooks run in Claude's shell (Git Bash on Windows).
config.claude.notify.description: Notifications from the Claude Code instances opened by AgentYard.
config.claude.notify.enumDescriptions.0: When one needs you (permission request or question).
config.claude.notify.enumDescriptions.1: Also when one finishes its turn.
config.claude.notify.enumDescriptions.2: No notifications (the status bar and the panel still show the state).

config.agentTerminalLocation.enumDescrip: As an editor tab beside the code (a new column if needed).
In the panel, split with the other agent terminal of the same worktree.
Tasks in the panel; interactive sessions beside the code.
config.agentTerminalFocus.description: Whether a newly opened agent terminal takes the focus.
config.agentTerminalFocus.enumDescriptio: Interactive sessions take the focus; agents opened with a task open in the background.
Never: the terminal opens without leaving where you are.
config.agentFollowEditor.description: When you open a file of another worktree, bring its agent terminal in the panel to the front (without taking the focus).
config.claude.answerFromNotification.mar: Adds **Allow** and **Deny** to the notification of a permission request, answering it without going to the terminal (Enter accepts the highlighted option, Esc denies). Experimental: depends on the Claude Code prompt.
config.claude.onSessionEnd.description: What to do with the terminal when a Claude Code session ends (/exit, Ctrl+C twice).
config.claude.onSessionEnd.enumDescripti: Offer to resume the session in the same terminal or close it (not when you are looking at it).
Keep the terminal open, without asking.
config.claude.connectIde.markdownDescrip: Opens Claude Code with `--ide`, connecting it to VS Code on startup (diffs in the editor, selection and problems shared). Needs the Claude Code extension and the worktree inside the workspace.
config.claude.ideWorkspace.markdownDescr: Claude only connects to VS Code (`/ide`) when its folder is inside the workspace. When a Claude opens in a worktree outside it (and the Claude Code extension is installed), offer to add the worktree as a workspace folder.
